items.description: classmate-visual-qa's first calibration pass flagged a wordmark color inconsistency (the 'Class' half of 'ClassMate' renders a different blue on Landing vs. the Teacher sign-in gate) on js/ui/views/LandingView.js, a file with active, uncommitted edits from the user's own separate work session (WORK-0001). It is unknown whether this finding describes something the user's in-progress edit already fixes, something it introduced, or something pre-existing and unrelated. Not investigated further, per the Supervisor's role of recording rather than resolving.
items.notes: Do not treat this finding as a bug report against the user's in-progress work without checking with them first - the file is mid-edit and this may be moot, already-known, or unrelated to whatever they're changing. Reconfirmed by WORK-0005 (2026-09-13): the same wordmark color difference (Landing vs. Teacher sign-in gate) is visible identically at 1440px, 1024px, 768px, and 390px, i.e. it is not a responsive/viewport-dependent artifact. Still not investigated further and still not to be treated as a settled bug against the user's in-progress LandingView.js edit without checking with them first. Re-checked at WORK-0006 (2026-09-13): a request to re-run the same 4-route/4-viewport Visual QA scope was evaluated rather than re-delegated, since WORK-0001 affected files (including LandingView.js) were confirmed unchanged since WORK-0005 via git status. This conflict record therefore still stands unresolved and unchanged in substance — no new investigation of the wordmark color itself was performed. Reconfirmed a third time, independently, by WORK-0013 (2026-09-13, Bento-consistency-specific audit pass): the same 'Class' half of 'ClassMate' wordmark color difference (Landing vs. Teacher sign-in gate) reproduces identically at all 4 widths, labeled there as FINDING-A01 (WARNING, OBSERVED). This is the same underlying issue, not a new one - cross-checked against this record before filing. Status remains 'potential' and unresolved; still not to be treated as a settled bug against WORK-0001's in-progress LandingView.js edit without checking with the user first. CORRECTION (2026-09-14, same pre-commit pass, before anything above was ever committed): the entry immediately above this one (dated 2026-09-14, status 'resolved', resolution citing commit a0aeafc) was wrong and has been reverted. That verification pass checked only INTERNAL consistency on the Landing page itself (wordmark vs. Teacher portal button vs. Teacher icon, all within js/ui/views/LandingView.js / .landing-view__* CSS classes) - it never actually compared Landing against the separate Teacher sign-in gate (js/ui/views/LoginView.js / .login-view__* CSS classes), which is what this conflict has tracked since WORK-0004 first raised it. Direct CSS inspection performed as part of this correction (css/styles.css) confirms the cross-page divergence this conflict tracks is still present, unchanged: .landing-view__title-class computes to #5ea5d9 (WORK-0001's new value) while .login-view__title-class computes to #1565c0 (untouched by WORK-0001) - two clearly different blues. Per css/styles.css's own code comment on the Landing change (immediately above .landing-view__title-class): the color change was 'Scoped deliberately to just this screen's title/Teacher Portal button/icon ... not login-view__title-class or any other blue in the app, per explicit instruction not to change every occurrence of blue site-wide' - i.e. this divergence was a deliberate scope boundary for that round of work, not an oversight WORK-0001 missed. Status, resolved_at, and resolution have been reverted to potential/null/null accordingly. This does not change WORK-0001's own status (still 'completed' - the work itself was genuinely finished and pushed; only the conflict-resolution claim about it was wrong). See reports/session-reports.md REPORT-0014 for the full correction account.

items.description: The term 'Concept' names at least three structurally unrelated things across the two codebases, with no shared ID space: (1) ClassMate's curriculum-pipeline Concept (Unit -> Concept, see ARCHITECTURE.md in classroom-tracker), (2) Learning Hub's RepositoryConcept (concepts/{conceptId}, Firestore, learner/exploration-facing), and (3) Learning Hub's legacy in-memory MissionConcept (never persisted). A ClassMate-side 'conceptId' does not resolve in Learning Hub, and vice versa, without the not-yet-built learningHubConcept mapping field. This is an architectural ambiguity, not a bug in either codebase, and not something either team did wrong.
items.notes: By explicit user instruction: record this and do not attempt to resolve it yet. Any future task in either repo that touches a 'Concept'-named entity, or any cross-project work involving conceptId, must check this record and cross-reference cross-project/dependencies.md before assuming shared meaning. Do not close or resolve this record without a real, ratified decision (see decisions-log.md, DEC-PENDING items) establishing how - or whether - the meanings are reconciled.
